name: Cowra

what_it_is.fact: Town of about 8,250 people (Wikipedia; WV says ~10,000) on the Lachlan River in the Central West of NSW, ~310 km west of Sydney and 189 km north of Canberra, at the junction of the Mid-Western Highway, Olympic Highway and Lachlan Valley Way. Site of a WWII POW camp and the 1944 Breakout; Japanese garden and Japanese war cemetery draw visitors. Cowra wine region (40+ vineyards around Cowra, Billimari and Canowindra) per Wikivoyage.

coordinates.note: Wikivoyage centre; matches placement.json. Visitor Information Centre is at Olympic Park, Mid-Western Highway (WV: +61 2 6342 4333).

rank.reason: Sizable regional town / local base; Japanese Garden is a regional draw but not a country highlight (COVERAGE.md rank 5 'local base'; rank 4 is arguable given the garden and Breakout story).

facts: Cowra Japanese Garden and Cultural Centre bills itself 'the largest Japanese garden in the Southern Hemisphere', 12.5 acres (operator claim, attribute if used).
Designed by Japanese architect Ken Nakajima as a kaiyu-shiki strolling garden; symbolises reconciliation and peace after WWII.
Cultural Centre with artworks and artefacts, gift shop and cafe; cherry blossoms in spring, autumn colour (Koyo Matsuri), misty winter.
whyVisit_candidates.photo_hint: Commons: Cowra Japanese Garden and Australian bush (3380052178).jpg (skeptic-accepted as the spot photo; use a different file for the reason, since three whyVisit photos must differ from the spot-free header rule only for header).

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Walk the site of the 1944 Cowra Breakout
facts: On 5 August 1944, 1,104 Japanese POWs escaped from the Cowra camp: the largest prison escape of WWII; 4 Australians and 231 Japanese died. Leaders ordered no attacks on civilians; none were hurt.

POW Camp Site, Sakura Avenue, open all hours, free (WV). Japanese War Cemetery on Doncaster Drive (-33.8017,148.6917) is the only Japanese war cemetery in Australia, ceded to Japan 1963; Australian cemetery beside it (WV).
POW Theatre hologram ('Clare') in the Cowra Visitor Information Centre, 9AM-5PM, donation (WV, may be dated).
whyVisit_candidates.photo_hint: Commons: Graves at the Japanese War Cemetery, Cowra August 2020.jpg (skeptic accepted for the spot; weak). Sakura Avenue or the camp-site file would be a distinct choice for whyVisit; unchecked.

facts: Canowindra, ~32 km north of Cowra on the Belubula River, is a historic township; curving Gaskill Street is partly an urban conservation area and 34 buildings/features are on the NSW State Heritage Register.

A 1955 roadworks find uncovered a Devonian (>360 Ma) slab of 114 fish fossils; the Age of Fishes Museum displays the finds. Operator page: open 10am-3.45pm Thursday to Monday, closed Tue/Wed, open 7 days in NSW school holidays.
Wikipedia calls Canowindra the 'Ballooning Capital of Australia'; balloon flights run at sunrise and the last hour before sunset during the April Balloon Challenge.
whyVisit_candidates.note: Recommended third reason is the Age of Fishes/Canowindra town (a year-round draw), with ballooning as a seasonal addition, not the reason itself. Age of Fishes Museum is held pending photo in placement.json, so the reason's photo must be a Canowindra view or fossil photo (Commons, unverified).

alternative_reason: Cowra wine region (40+ vineyards, Chardonnay since the 1970s) per WV, but skeptic rejected it as a spot; usable as a short sentence in the description only.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: Garden entry is $22 adult, $17 concession/local, $12 child, $52 family; open 8:30am-5pm daily; festival-day prices differ. Not a flat garden (mobility), dogs on a lead welcome except during Sakura Matsuri.

Public transport is thin: WV lists two NSW TrainLink coach services a day from Bathurst/Lithgow and no airport in town (nearest scheduled flights Orange, Parkes, Bathurst); plan to drive, ~1.5 h from Bathurst or Orange, with Canowindra reached by car. (WV timetable dated, so say 'coach only' not times.)

Age of Fishes Museum in Canowindra is closed Tuesday and Wednesday outside NSW school holidays (open Thu-Mon 10am-3.45pm), so time the Canowindra day accordingly; book accommodation early for festival weekends (Sakura Matsuri late Sept, Balloon Challenge April).

sakura_matsuri.fact: Annual one-day festival at the Cowra Japanese Garden marking the cherry blossom: Sat 26 Sep 2026, Sat 27 Sep 2025, Sat 28 Sep 2024 (late September, a Saturday). Blossoms usually flower from mid/late September to mid-October (search summary; weather-dependent). 2027 date not found.

koyo_matsuri.fact: Autumn leaf festival at the garden exists (listed as 'Koyo Matsuri 2026' in site navigation); dates not fetched.

canowindra_balloon_challenge.fact: Canowindra International Balloon Challenge, billed as Australia's largest ballooning event, held each April; 2026 edition 11-19 April, community glow 18 April. 2020 cancelled (COVID), 2021 ran 26 Apr-1 May.

bestMonths.reasoning: Own inference, not a travel-guide consensus: southern-hemisphere autumn (Mar-May; April balloons) and spring (Sep-Nov; cherry blossom late Sep-Oct). Climate per Wikipedia: max ~32C in high summer, ~14C mid-winter with frequent frost and even snow, rainfall ~598 mm spread through the year. No guidebook best-time statement found.
